title: Your First Weekend at Emmanuel College, Shared as Cards
description: A low-key first-weekend sequence built around campus gathering spaces, student resources, food, movement, and an outdoor stop across the street.

cards.title: Start at the Jean Yawkey Center
cards.subtitle: First stop: campus hub
cards.notes: Use the staffed front desk as an orientation point, then take a lap through the atrium, common areas, gymnasium, and dining level.
cards.short_summary: A practical first look at Emmanuel’s central student space.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel identifies the Jean Yawkey Center as its student center, dining hall, gymnasium, fitness center, and gathering place.
cards.access_notes: Campus building; confirm current building access procedures with Emmanuel.

cards.title: Check Engage for a current event
cards.subtitle: Next: find a campus activity
cards.notes: Open Emmanuel’s Engage platform, filter for an interest or date, and use the listing details to decide whether an upcoming event fits your weekend.
cards.short_summary: The college’s portal for organizations and upcoming events.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel says Engage lets students learn about organizations, join them, and see planned events.
cards.access_notes: Online platform; individual events may have their own attendance requirements.

cards.title: Have a meal in Marian Hall
cards.subtitle: Midday: Jean Yawkey Center
cards.notes: Review the dining options, then plan a meal at the main dining room if your meal plan or payment arrangement covers entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel describes Marian Hall Dining Room in the Jean Yawkey Center as its main dining facility with buffet-style dining.
cards.access_notes: Dining access and payment depend on current meal-plan or payment arrangements.

cards.title: Pause at the Muddy River Café
cards.subtitle: Afternoon: Eisner Administration Building
cards.notes: Stop by the first-floor café for a grab-and-go option, then use the patio outside when conditions and campus access allow.
cards.short_summary: A named on-campus café beside outdoor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel places the Muddy River Café on the first floor of the Eisner Administration Building and lists its food offerings.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; verify current café availability before visiting.

cards.title: Settle into Cardinal Cushing Library
cards.subtitle: Late afternoon: study or reset
cards.notes: Choose a table or individual carrel, explore the first two floors, and ask library staff about research or computer-station support.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with spaces for solo and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel says the first two floors of Cardinal Cushing Library provide seating, tables, carrels, computer stations, and library staff assistance.
cards.source_title: Study Spots & Library at Emmanuel College
cards.access_notes: Campus library; confirm current access and service hours with Emmanuel.

cards.title: Find the St. Julie media center
cards.subtitle: Early evening: St. Julie Hall
cards.notes: Walk through St. Julie Hall’s first floor and use the Media Center as a named destination while you get familiar with its study areas.
cards.short_summary: A named media center within St. Julie Hall’s shared first-floor spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel lists the Margaret L. McKenna '83 Media Center among the student study spaces on the first floor of St. Julie Hall.
cards.source_title: Study Spots & Library at Emmanuel College
cards.access_notes: Campus space; confirm current building access and any equipment-use requirements.

cards.title: Try the Yawkey Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Movement break: Jean Yawkey Center
cards.notes: Bring your Emmanuel ID, check in at the appropriate building desk, and choose a workout suited to the available cardio or strength equipment.
cards.short_summary: One of Emmanuel’s campus fitness facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel states that students have access to the Yawkey Fitness Center and describes its cardio, circuit-training, and free-weight equipment.
cards.access_notes: Student access; Emmanuel directs commuters to check in with a building front desk and leave an Emmanuel ID while working out.

cards.title: See the Emmanuel College Chapel
cards.subtitle: Quiet stop: Eisner Administration Building
cards.notes: Visit respectfully, taking time to notice this central campus space; check with the College before planning around a service or private event.
cards.short_summary: A historic chapel at the center of the Eisner Administration Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel describes the College Chapel as being at the center of the Eisner Administration Building and as the site of more than a century of liturgies, weddings, and campus traditions.
cards.access_notes: Respectful campus access only; confirm availability around services and events.

cards.title: Meet up on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Evening: outdoor campus gathering space
cards.notes: Use the Quad as a simple meet-up point, and check Engage or campus communications for any currently scheduled outdoor program before heading over.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus setting used for student gatherings and activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel’s 2025 orientation schedule located group activities on the EC Quad and listed Saints at Night in the JYC Atrium/Quad.
cards.source_title: 2025 Summer Orientation: Student Schedule | Emmanuel College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; events and access vary by date and weather.

cards.title: Finish with a walk at Roberto Clemente Field
cards.subtitle: Across the street in the Back Bay Fens
cards.notes: Cross at a marked intersection, then use the public track for a walk or jog while respecting scheduled athletics, permits, and other users.
cards.short_summary: A city-owned field and public track directly across from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Emmanuel says Roberto Clemente Field is across the street from campus and that its all-weather track remains open to the public year-round for walking and jogging.
cards.access_notes: The track is open to the public for recreational walking and jogging; field use is managed and permitted through Boston Parks and Recreation.
